guardian.description:
‘Mastermind’ Dawie Groenewald given fine of 2m rand or four-year jail term almost 16 years after arrest

Two traffickers of rhino horns have been sentenced by a South African court in what police said was the world’s largest such case, partly bringing to an end an almost two-decade legal saga.

Dawie Groenewald and Tielman Erasmus had faced more than 1,700 charges ranging from illegally hunting and dehorning rhinos to racketeering and money laundering.

Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada told reporters last week that her husband, who is Black, had been repeatedly stopped by police while driving.

For years, healthcare staff in the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador have felt overworked and underappreciated. Turnover, burnout and thinning resources were pushing workers in the sector to a breaking point.

Major operation launched after spate of pet thefts in Ho Chi Minh City, according to local media

Police in Vietnam have rescued more than 400 cats in a bust of a cat meat crime ring in Ho Chi Minh City, according to animal welfare groups and local media reports.

More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

rfi.title: 'Brexit hasn't gone wrong': an advocate’s view of leaving the EU, 10 years on
rfi.description: Ten years after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains one of the most contested political decisions in recent British history. While its economic and political effects continue to be debated, its legacy is increasingly shaped by diverging interpretations of sovereignty, trade and Britain’s place in the world. RFI spoke to a Brexit supporter Robert Oulds, director of the Bruges Group about what has changed.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

lemonde.description: Les Bleus ont remporté contre l’Irak (3-0), lundi, une rencontre qui s’est étirée pendant plus de trois heures en raison des conditions météorologiques à Philadelphie. Kylian Mbappé, Michael Olise et Ousmane Dembélé ont tous trois été déterminants.

L’affaire, emblématique de #MeToo, s’était close par un non-lieu en 2021, confirmé par la cour d’appel de Paris en mai 2022, puis par la Cour de cassation en juin 2023.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : la France qualifiée en seizièmes de finale au bout de la nuit
france24fr.description: Avec une deuxième victoire en deux matches, les Bleus ont validé leur ticket pour les seizièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde. S’ils n’ont jamais vraiment été embêtés par l’Irak (3-0), les Bleus ont surtout été perturbés par l’orage au-dessus de Philadelphie, qui a interrompu la rencontre pendant presque deux heures entre la première et la seconde période.

france24fr.title: “C’était magnifique” : les supporters français réagissent après la victoire contre l’Irak
france24fr.description: La France de Kylian Mbappé a arraché lundi à Philadelphie sa qualification pour les 16e de finale du Mondial. Les Bleus ont battu l'Irak 3-0 lors d’une rencontre interrompue durant plus de deux heures en raison des orages et des intempéries. Après cette partie pas comme les autres, les supporters français sur place ont réagi au micro de France 24.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Norvège (3-2) Sénégal, les supporters sénégalais entre déception et espoir
france24fr.description: Battu 3-2 par la Norvège, le Sénégal voit ses chances de qualification se compliquer. À Dakar, les supporters sont partagés entre déception et espoir. Malgré le revers, beaucoup continuent de croire aux Lions pour la suite de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Algérie encore en vie après sa victoire face à la Jordanie
Mondial 2026 : l'Algérie encore en vie après sa victoire face à la Jordanie
france24fr.description: Après sa lourde défaite face à l'Argentine, l'Algérie s'est rattrapée en dominant la Jordanie (2-1) mardi au Levi's Stadium de Santa Clara en Californie. D'abord menés au score, les Fennecs sont revenus dans le match sur deux coups de pied arrêtés victorieux en seconde période.

france24fr.title: France-Irak interrompu : les spectateurs philosophes au micro de France 24
france24fr.description: ⁠Le début de ​la seconde période du match de Coupe du monde entre l'équipe de ​France et l'Irak a été retardé de deux heures et douze minutes en raison d'#orages à Philadelphie. Les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 y étaient.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'Iran ne prévoit pas de laisser l'AIEA inspecter les sites bombardés
france24fr.description: L’Iran a démenti mardi les propos du vice-président américain, J.D. Vance, sur un retour des inspecteurs de l’AIEA, assurant n’avoir pris "aucun nouvel engagement" après des discussions avec Washington en Suisse, et a réaffirmé sa volonté de garder le contrôle du détroit d’Ormuz malgré l’allègement annoncé des sanctions pétrolières américaines. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Norvège en 16es de finale, le Sénégal au bord de l'élimination
Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: Un match de la France à rallonge, une qualification bleue pour les seizièmes de finale, Messi recordman du nombre de buts en Coupe du monde… Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Norvège en seizièmes de finale, le Sénégal au bord de l'élimination
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal s'est incliné dans le choc face à la Norvège (2-3) lundi au MetLife Stadium dans le New Jersey, quelques jours après une première défaite concédée face à la France (1-3) dans la même enceinte. Avec toujours aucun point au compteur, les Lions de la Teranga devront réagir lors de la troisième journée pour espérer se qualifier, alors que la Norvège est assurée de disputer les seizièmes de finale et jouera la première place du groupe face à la France.

france24fr.title: Jordanie - Algérie : les Fennecs dominent l'Al-Nashama et peuvent encore croire aux 16e de finale
france24fr.description: D'abord battue par l'Argentine, l'Algérie a retrouvé des couleurs face à la Jordanie, mardi. Les Fennecs ont inscrit deux buts sur corner en deuxième mi-temps après avoir été menés au score. Revivez ce match de Coupe du monde grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: En Bolivie, les barrages routiers progressivement levés après sept semaines de crise
france24fr.description: Les derniers barrages routiers étaient progressivement en train d'être levés lundi en Bolivie après l'annonce d'une trêve temporaire par l'ancien président Evo Morales, trois jours après la proclamation de l'état d'exception visant à mettre fin à plus de sept semaines de contestation.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RD Congo : plus de 1000 cas confirmés et au moins 250 décès
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’épidémie d’Ebola poursuit sa progression. Les autorités sanitaires recensent désormais 1 003 cas confirmés et 254 décès au dernier bilan, franchissant pour la première fois le seuil des mille contaminations.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la France foudroie l'Irak et se qualifie pour les 16es de finale
Mondial 2026 : la France foudroie l'Irak et se qualifie pour les seizièmes de finale
france24fr.description: Malgré un match perturbé par un orage et interrompu pendant plus de deux heures à la mi-temps, l'équipe de France a balayé lundi sans difficulté l'Irak (3-0) à Philadelphie pour son deuxième match disputé lors de ce Mondial. Le capitaine français Kylian Mbappé s'est offert un doublé (14e, 54e) pour devenir le second meilleur buteur de l'histoire de la Coupe du monde à égalité avec l'Allemand Miroslav Klose (16 buts).

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : 54 départements en vigilance rouge, un niveau d’alerte inédit
france24fr.description: Plus de la moitié de la France est placée mardi en vigilance rouge canicule alors que des températures records continuent d'être enregistrées. Les autorités redoutent les effets sanitaires de cet épisode de chaleur exceptionnel, dont la durée reste encore incertaine.

zeit.title: Brände: Brand in Jevenstedt - Ein Mensch schwer verletzt
Rentenreform: »Es gibt einen großen Unterschied zu Riester«
zeit.description: Der Ökonom Jörg Rocholl ist Mitglied der Rentenkommission. Hier erklärt er, warum der Staat Geld für die Rente an der Börse anlegen soll – und wem das helfen würde.

Einzelhandel: Schaden durch Ladendiebstähle übertrifft Drei-Milliarden-Marke
zeit.description: Der deutsche Einzelhandel meldet einen Rekordschaden ​durch Ladendiebstahl. 2025 wurden dort Waren im Wert von drei Milliarden Euro gestohlen. Die Dunkelziffer ist hoch.

zeit.title: Arbeitsmarkt: Fast ein Drittel aller Erwerbsfähigen kommt bis 2040 ins Rentenalter
zeit.description: Die Babyboomer sind kurz vor der Rente, arbeiten zum Großteil aber noch. Bis 2040 werden sie fehlen – und eine große Lücke in den Arbeitsmarkt reißen.

zeit.title: Finanzierung der Rente: Bundesregierung will alle Vorschläge der Rentenkommission umsetzen
zeit.description: Kanzler Friedrich Merz lobt die Vorschläge der Rentenkommission und kündigt eine »zügige« Umsetzung »aller Elemente« an. In der Koalition sei man sich einig.

zeit.title: Statistisches Bundesamt: Jeder Fünfte kann sich keine Woche Urlaub leisten
zeit.description: Eine Woche Urlaub ist in Deutschland für ein Fünftel der Menschen zu teuer. Besonders betroffen sind laut Statistischem Bundesamt Alleinstehende und Alleinerziehende.

zeit.title: EU-Klimaziele: Logistikbranche braucht in Zukunft achtmal so viel Strom
zeit.description: Der Lkw-Verkehr soll zügig elektrifiziert werden. Wissenschaftler haben nun ermittelt, dass der Strombedarf höher sein wird als in der Chemie- und Stahlproduktion.

zeit.title: Autobahnausbau: Verbände fordern Verzicht auf Autobahn-Neubauten
zeit.description: Statt neue Bundesstraßen und Autobahnen zu bauen, solle man die alten erhalten, sagen Verbände. So ließen sich Milliarden sparen, die anderswo dringend gebraucht würden.

observador.title: Roménia continua sem novo ministro após derrota de Vestea
observador.description: Depois dos insuficientes 189 votos, o liberal Adrian Vestea alertou para os impactos dos "quarenta e sete dias sem Governo", altura em que o Parlamento romeno destituiu o Governo pró-UE de Bolojan.

observador.title: Sindicato da Polícia denuncia más condições de trabalho
observador.description: Associação Sindical dos Profissionais da Polícia considerou situação na Unidade de Fronteiras um "ciclo de desorganização", apontando para "carências críticas" e incerteza sobre futuro profissional.

observador.title: Peru. Candidato pede anulação de votos no estrangeiro
observador.description: O candidato da esquerda Roberto Sánchez, que está prestes a perder para Keiko Fujimori (direita) nas presidenciais do Peru, interpôs um recurso para anular os votos do estrangeiro.

observador.title: Reservistas de Taiwan passam a cumprir treino de 14 dias
observador.description: Taiwan aboliu o sistema que permitia aos reservistas escolher entre dois modelos de treino e passou a exigir um programa intensivo de 14 dias, visando reforçar a preparação do exército.

observador.title: Governo talibã em Bruxelas para falar sobre refugiados
observador.description: Governo talibã do Afeganistão vai reunir-se pela primeira vez com representantes da UE desde que assumiu o poder, em 2021. As conversações serão estritamente técnicas, sobre questões como migração.

observador.title: Companhia chinesa retoma voo direto entre Pequim e Lisboa
observador.description: A companhia aérea chinesa Beijing Capital Airlines inaugurou uma nova rota direta entre o Aeroporto Internacional de Pequim Daxing e Lisboa que vai operar durante cerca de três meses.

observador.title: Somos oficialmente 11 milhões. Aguenta coração (e Ventura)
observador.description: Somos 11,6 milhões e a pizza per capita encolheu. Enquanto Ventura faz teatro na AR com reformas "absurdas", Messi ensina como marcar golos até a andar.

observador.title: CATL quer instalar mais de 30 estações de troca de baterias
observador.description: A chinesa CATL, maior fabricante mundial de baterias para veículos elétricos, planeia instalar mais de 30 estações de troca de baterias para camiões na Europa até 2035.

observador.title: 9h. Manifesto dos 50+ exige prazos para magistrados
observador.description: O Manifesto dos 50+ alerta para um cenário de “descontrolo e falta de gestão no Ministério Público”. Ainda, a cultura e os hábitos dos uzbeques e as temperaturas elevadas na Europa.

observador.title: Chinesa JD prevê substituição de 700 mil estafetas por robôs
observador.description: O presidente da gigante chinesa do comércio eletrónico JD.com alertou que os cerca de 700 mil estafetas da empresa serão substituídos por robôs "mais cedo ou mais tarde".

observador.title: Reino Unido "irritado" com decisão da UE de adiar a cimeira
observador.description: António Costa, presidente do Conselho Europeu, anunciou que cimeira prevista para julho seria adiada. Decisão caiu como surpresa em Downing Street, revela o Financial Times.

observador.title: Autoridades patrulham espelho de água do Lincoln Memorial
observador.description: Autoridades patrulham a estrutura em redor do espelho de água do Lincoln Memorial, enquanto a administração Trump tenta corrigir falhas na renovação a tempo de celebrar 250.º aniversário da nação.

observador.title: Transformar dados em obras de arte
observador.description: Le_Brimet é um dos oradores do Data with Purpose Summit que acontece dia 25 de junho, em Oeiras. O artista conversa sobre a utilização de dados para criar as suas obras.

observador.title: Manifesto dos 50+ exige prazos obrigatórios para magistrados
observador.description: Grupo exige o fim dos prazos "meramente indicativos" para o Estado e critica "normalização dos abusos" e a "inércia política" face à lentidão dos processos — como o caso Influencer e Tutti-Fruti.

observador.title: Dia 13 do Mundial-2026. É dia de Portugal-Uzbequistão
observador.description: Depois da noite em que Messi voltou a brilhar com a Argentina e das vitórias de França, Noruega e Argélia, hoje Portugal volta a entrar em campo no NRG Stadium.

observador.title: Em Castro Daire, o junco protegia da chuva e do frio
observador.description: A tradição das capas "caroças" que, em tempo, abrigam os castrenses, é mantida pelos grupos folclóricos. Já a capucha de burel resistiu mais facilmente à evolução da indumentária.

observador.title: Apoiantes de Evo Morales suspendem protestos contra Bolívia
observador.description: Os apoiantes do ex-líder boliviano Evo Morales anunciaram que vão suspender os protestos que exigem a demissão do Presidente Rodrigo Paz, após mais de um mês e meio de bloqueios de estradas.

observador.title: Descoberta estrutura ritual maia com 2000 anos na Guatemala
observador.description: Equipa científica descobriu uma estrutura ritual maia única no sítio pré-hispânico de El Tigre, no norte da Guatemala, que fornece dados sobre as complexas práticas cerimoniais e padrões sociais.

nzz.description: In mehreren Kantonen fordert die Politik, den Einwohnern Überschüsse in Form von Rabatten zurückzugeben. Ein erster Kanton will die Idee nun in die Tat umsetzen.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - Wie Libanon zum Zankapfel zwischen den USA und Israel geworden ist
nzz.description: Israel will sich weder von den USA noch von Iran die Bedingungen für einen Frieden in Libanon diktieren lassen. Doch genau das spaltet das wichtige Bündnis mit den Amerikanern.

nzz.description: Die Briten wünschen sich einen Sozialstaat wie in Deutschland, der durch Steuern und Abgaben wie in den USA finanziert werden soll. Das geht nicht auf.

nzz.description: Ministerpräsident Sánchez sieht sich einer beispiellosen Fülle von Gerichtsprozessen in seinem unmittelbaren Umfeld gegenüber. Seine Frau muss am Mittwoch sogar ihren Reisepass abgeben.

nzz.description: Österreichs stärkste Partei sorgt für Kontroversen mit einem Lied, das Ausschaffungen feiert. Sie banalisiert damit einen rechtsextrem konnotierten Begriff, der anderen Rechtsaussenparteien zu radikal ist.

nzz.description: Die Geschichte der Träger des Ordens des Weissen Adlers könnte wechselhafter und widersprüchlicher kaum sein. Die Gründe dafür liegen in unsicheren politischen Grosswetterlagen. Die Aberkennung des Ordens für Wolodimir Selenski reiht sich passend ins Bild.

spiegel.title: Studie zu Gewalt an Berliner Schulen: Viele Lehrkräfte sehen Gewalt als großes Problem
spiegel.description: Viele Berliner Lehrkräfte betrachten Gewalt in der eigenen Schule als großes Problem, zeigt eine neue Studie. Co-Autor und Schulforscher Ullrich Bauer erklärt, was die Ergebnisse bedeuten – und was ihn überrascht hat.

spiegel.title: Wahlen im Osten: Die CDU braucht die Linkspartei - Kommentar

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz will Renten-Vorschläge vollständig umsetzen
spiegel.description: Die Rentenexperten haben der Bundesregierung ihre Reformvorschläge übergeben. Kanzler Merz erklärt, »alle Elemente« rasch umsetzen zu wollen. Arbeitsministerin Bas lobt das Konzept als »Gesamtkunstwerk«.

spiegel.title: Rente: Das sagen die Rentenexperten zu ihren Vorschlägen

spiegel.title: Russlands Krieg gegen Ukraine: Ukrainische Angriffe verschärfen Treibstoffknappheit

spiegel.title: Renten-Reform: So soll die neue Schweden-Rente funktionieren

spiegel.title: Paris: Wie mir Exil-Iraner halfen, bayerische Trachtenstrümpfe zu finden - Kolumne

spiegel.description: Erstaunlich viele Lehrkräfte glauben nach wie vor, dass sie im Klassenzimmer politisch absolut neutral sein müssen, zeigt das neue Schulbarometer. Dabei sind sie verpflichtet, für die Demokratie einzustehen.

phys-org.title: First quantum biosensor can detect rapid, invisible changes in cells
phys-org.description: In the development of diseases such as muscular dystrophy, cancer, Ebola and dengue, numerous chemical reactions take place within and between cells that contribute to disease progression. These changes can occur in less than the blink of an eye—within microseconds or faster—making them difficult to analyze. Quantum sensing offers a way to monitor these changes, helping researchers determine when, where and how rapid biological processes occur.

phys-org.title: Social inequality can harm the foundations of society
phys-org.description: Can economic inequality threaten liberal societies? This question lies at the heart of the POLAR project led by Markus Gangl, a sociologist at Goethe University Frankfurt. Several publications examining different aspects of the issue shed light on how trust in democracy, belief in meritocracy and perceptions of equal opportunity are changing.

A large share of the fruit and vegetables we eat have traveled across the globe before they reach store shelves here at home. But many millions of tons are lost every year before they get that far.

phys-org.title: What shapes young lives most? Everyday wins, relationships and school outrank crises

A study by the University of Zurich (UZH) shows that adolescents and young adults primarily cite positive, everyday developmental steps as formative events, for example, school and apprenticeships, friendships, first relationships, travel, and moving out of their parents' home. UZH researchers evaluated open-ended written responses from 1,442 participants in a long-term study. Each participant was surveyed at ages 15, 17, 20 and 24.

phys-org.title: Mosquito-borne viruses avoid killing hosts by limiting protein output, study reveals

Europe is no longer an exception, and autochthonous infections have already been recorded in Spain.

phys-org.title: Leaf-based fluorescence test speeds search for plant gene-editing targets

phys-org.title: Making sense of Mars' tiny moon Phobos
phys-org.description: Mars' innermost moon, Phobos, has long puzzled planetary scientists, who have continually debated whether it's a captured asteroid or formed from debris after a giant impactor struck the Martian surface. The key to solving the mystery mainly rests with a better understanding of Phobos' internal structure, which unfortunately remains a "known unknown."

phys-org.title: Women negotiate as effectively as men—but leave people happier

Recently, a research team in Korea brought this possibility one step closer to reality.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway

But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.
